decisions: Guided Launch replaces the first-run tooltip tour with an idea-first two-column setup flow using Nexus dark surfaces and restrained purple accents. New accounts describe their own idea before Roblox linking, receive beginner Studio setup with a fresh baseplate default, and continue in a dedicated Plan conversation with a compact PlanÃ¢â‚¬â€œBuildÃ¢â‚¬â€œTry it checklist. Studio application and user-confirmed playtest success remain distinct; setup screenshots must be verified before display.

The AI model picker follows a compact IDE selector pattern: search first, a minimal Nexus Auto row, 3-5 dynamic recommendations, then one continuous provider-grouped catalogue. Rows stay 36-42px tall with a single optional capability descriptor, subtle free-tier locks, checkmark selection, and no per-row billing, context-window, or usage-multiplier copy.

Planning remains conversational in chat without an active-step checklist. Reviewable plans use a compact overview, named execution stages, deterministic semantic flowcharts, and structured file or Studio-target tags; @ file references appear as removable composer context while the full source is fetched only when needed.

Roblox UI Creator inherits the Agent workspace design contract: Nexus dark surfaces, --nx-* and --ds-* tokens, typography, spacing, radii, controls, status feedback, focus treatment, motion, composer behavior, and responsive drawers. It remains a dense preview-first authoring workspace with Chat/Layers on the left, an unobstructed device canvas in the center, Properties/Actions/Assets plus checkpoint history on the right, and rendered Roblox UI that may use each design's own tokens.

Current Studio activity may also appear in a compact status bar above the composer, but it never replaces or filters the inline live stream; status stages, display-safe reasoning, tool actions, file writes and code excerpts, reconnect states, and streamed response text remain visible together in the conversation while work is running.

Signed-in header account controls are avatar-first: show the connected Roblox profile image when available, otherwise the authenticated provider photo, then identity initials; keep the full identity and plan details inside the accessible account menu.
Settings sidebar icons use short, tab-specific hover and keyboard-focus animations inspired by the 21st Animated Sidebar pattern; motion is disabled when reduced motion is requested.

The Settings desktop navigation uses a compact 260px application sidebar with a small identity block, restrained section label, icon-led rounded rows, and a soft purple selected state while preserving the existing tab order and behavior.
Settings is a full-width application page with a viewport-spanning header, persistent desktop navigation rail, and flexible content pane; mobile retains the section drawer.
Settings Usage uses an accessible included-usage meter, a concise KPI strip, 7-day and 30-day trend views, workflow distribution, and searchable expandable events backed by real usage records.

Settings uses a premium control-center hierarchy with grouped searchable navigation, visible section titles and inline guidance, restrained elevated panels, actionable readiness rows, and deep analytics only in Plan and usage.

Financial catalog v2 uses three responsive Free/Pro/Team cards with Pro recommended at USD 14.99 and 9 monthly Nexus Credits. Annual payment and monthly credit refresh are separate. Team stays visibly unreleased until verified. Billing is an account ledger, not another pricing grid; public copy never shows wholesale model costs or unverified social proof.
Downloads uses compact icon-led platform tabs and question-mark dev tips so only essential release and setup text remains visible.

The Evidence Stage uses five narrow-panel lenses: Files, Editor, Run, Assets, and Report. Empty states remain compact and actionable; Run uses searchable expandable real-event rows; Report separates summary, structure, and validation evidence, with Summary opening on a dense outcome ledger for delivery status, files, Studio services, run completion, QA, file types, and recorded issues.

Required Roblox setup reuses the compact Nexus auth ledger with an AccountÃ¢â‚¬â€œEmailÃ¢â‚¬â€œRoblox progress strip, an explicit standard-permission summary, one primary connection action, and inline retry/sign-out recovery instead of introducing a parallel wizard shell.

Creator refresh: compact dark Roblox workspace with purple accents; Obby, Simulator and Adventure artwork populate editable drafts; projects are created on first send. Assets are preview-led with advanced filters collapsed. Provider logos are bundled locally. Studio reconnects never show unsupported-release warnings until compatibility is verified.

UI Creator retains the supplied reference’s dark violet shell, 57px top bar, purple accents and project navigation. The approved continuous-session workflow replaces the sample preview and permanent inspector with a persistent AI conversation beside verified Pinevex renders, and a right Code / Files drawer. Generation starts without Studio; saved revisions, application, capture, render and review have separate honest statuses. No DOM or sample preview renderer.
